notes: The main --links path works for both backends, but the zip side reads every symlink member into memory with an unbounded ReadAll while listing, even when --links is off, so one bad member can stop the whole archive opening. LinkRemote does not add the suffix to a symlink whose name already ends in .rclonelink, which breaks the backend convention. A zip root pointing at a symlink produces a bogus '.rclonelink' object. The tests cover zip only, and the escape test relies on copy order.

Works for the common cases, but the zip reader opens and fully reads every symlink member into memory when the archive is read, with no size limit and even when links are being skipped (a DoS and fragility risk); LinkRemote wrongly refuses to double-suffix a symlink already named *.rclonelink; OpenLink does not clamp negative offsets; it adds shared helpers to archiver.go and squashfs has no tests.

This follows the reference design closely: symlinks are always suffixed, skipped with a notice when --links is off, and NewObject agrees with List. The zip side reads member data lazily, and the squashfs side has an explicit link Open path with range/seek clamping. The tests are thorough, covering both backends, an end-to-end sync copy, and the hostile-escape case. The main gaps are a squashfs root pointing at a symlink and a log message that names only --links, not -l.

Closely mirrors the reference: links flag captured at construction, suffix added to symlinks, the zip target streamed from the member, squashfs targets read from StatT, and NewObject reconciled with List; the (nil, nil) skip return is slightly awkward and a squashfs root pointing straight at a symlink is mishandled, but tests are thorough (zip, squashfs fixture, range/seek, literal .rclonelink, end-to-end copy and escape).
